newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ING Barings sees Brazil 1996 deficit 4.5 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings sees Brazil 1996 deficit 4.5 pct of GDP.

text.p: ING Barings has increased its forecast of Brazil's public sector operational deficit to 4.5 percent of gross domestic product, up from a previous prediction of 3.5 percent, ING Barings economist Mauro Schneider said.
The bank also saw "little room" for improvement in Brazil's fiscal situation in 1997 when the deficit would be close to this year's result, Schneider told Reuters.

The poor situation of the finances of Brazil's states was the main factor contributing to the deficit "which is worse than we originally thought and is approaching last year's (result)," Schneider said.

Brazil reported a public sector operational deficit of 5.0 percent in 1995. Government officials originally hoped to halve that figure in 1996 but Finance Minister Pedro Malan said in October the deficit would be around 3.5 percent of GDP.
The federal government was also unlikely to improve its fiscal performance in 1997, the economist said.
Federal workers are expected to be given pay rises of about 10 percent next year, after no rises in 1996, Schneider said.
And there was little chance of a fall in interest rates in 1997 comparable with the drop between 1995 and 1996 which helped the federal fiscal situation this year, he said.
"There is very little room for an improvement in the federal government as well (as in the states)," Schneider said.
